# Academic Summarization and Synthesis — Evidence-Preserving Protocol V1
Date: 2026-10-10
Status: supplemental reading/output procedure; subordinate to canonical thesis/evidence/citation authorities and existing universal scientific reading protocols.

## Purpose
Convert complex source documents into concise, source-faithful, verifiable research summaries without inventing findings, flattening important caveats or replacing full-text inspection. Trigger for an explicit request to summarize, condense, write a literature note, extract essential arguments or synthesize multiple papers. Do not automatically initiate lessons or exams.

## Four-stage method
1. PREVIEW: record document type, actual access level (full text vs abstract/excerpt), bibliographic identity, section architecture, research problem and purpose. A heading skim is not a full-text audit.
2. ANALYZE: read actively for central claim/question, methods, actual evidence, quantitative findings, comparison baseline, assumptions, uncertainties, limitations, conclusion, and stated applicability. Distinguish authors' claims from direct observations and analyst inference.
3. ORGANIZE: extract only meaning-critical propositions in a source trace table (claim | evidence type | page/section/eq/figure | qualifiers | status). Separate essential, supporting and nonessential information. No fixed highlighting percentage or assumed 80/20 law.
4. RECONSTRUCT AND VERIFY: explain substance in independent language, compress relationships rather than copy-editing source phrases, reopen the original and check every material claim, number, unit, method, qualification and citation. Record unsupported/unclear as OPEN rather than fill it in.

## Minimum output structure
Bibliographic identity and access status; 1–3 sentence main contribution; question/purpose; method or proof strategy; principal evidenced results; assumptions/limits; qualified conclusion and relevance to the user's question. Vary length with user intent. Where the source lacks an item, explicitly mark NOT_REPORTED or NOT_INSPECTED.
For science use IMRaD-informed reading without forcing a uniform template. For theory preserve definitions, assumptions, theorem statement, proof method and validity domain. For empirical science preserve design, controls, units, reported estimates and uncertainty. For modeling preserve states, inputs, boundaries, equations, coupling ports, scenarios, VVUQ status and measured service consequences. For standards distinguish normative requirement from commentary.

## Nonnegotiable semantic guards
- `may` != `does`; association != causality; numerical prediction != measurement; verification != validation; source conclusion != independently established fact.
- Preserve sign, units, denominator, dates, confidence/uncertainty, operational mode and scenario boundary where material.
- Do not infer evidence from abstract/figure thumbnail. Do not invent missing citations, data, equations, page numbers or source rights.
- Neutral summary and independent critique are separate labeled products. A claim of novelty requires source-aware closest-prior-art audit.
- For the active thesis distinguish common heat forcing from directional P→T_e or T_e→P mechanism; grid-side AC load influence from reverse electrical energy flow; physical state from functional capability, service, resilience and SDG indicator. Never convert expected impacts into achieved SDG targets.

## Summarization vs synthesis
One-source summary: reconstruct that source on its own terms.
Multi-source synthesis: first summarize sources separately, then build a comparison matrix including methods, assumptions, sample, mechanisms, findings, limitations and disagreements. Harmonize quantities only where definitions and conditions are genuinely comparable. Disagreement is an output, not a defect to conceal.

## Quality gates
Q1 exact source/version and access recorded.
Q2 dominant scientific question/contribution intact.
Q3 method, controls and evidence type accurate.
Q4 findings and quantitative statements checked against source.
Q5 assumptions, uncertainty and negative/null findings retained.
Q6 author's interpretation separated from expert inference and independent verification.
Q7 citation-level traceability for material claims.
Q8 independent paraphrasing, shortness proportional to task and readable organization.
If any material gate fails, status = PROVISIONAL; do not silently assert PASS.

## Academic methodological references (background, not thesis evidence)
- Purdue OWL, Quoting, Paraphrasing and Summarizing: https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/using_research/quoting_paraphrasing_and_summarizing/index.html
- Cornell Learning Strategies Center, Cornell note-taking: https://lsc.cornell.edu/how-to-study/taking-notes/cornell-note-taking-system/
- PRISMA 2020, reporting systematic reviews: https://www.prisma-statement.org/ (apply only to eligible review reporting, not all summaries)
